# Appwrite

Generated from [tokens.json](tokens.json) and [README.md](README.md) by the design-systems catalog tool. Do not edit this file: change the tokens through the package's builders, then run `make design-md` at the repository root.

It follows the DESIGN.md spec, version alpha. That format has no themes, no per-value provenance and only px, em and rem units, so this file holds the `light` theme alone with every alias resolved. [tokens.json](tokens.json) is the source of truth: it records where each value was read, holds the `dark` theme, and keeps the 0 tokens from these groups that DESIGN.md cannot hold (gradients, shadows, percentages, durations and other non-colour or non-px values).

## Overview

Good for: Developer-platform marketing: pinned-dark SvelteKit + Tailwind v4 site, brand-pink CTAs and gradient hero text, hairline-bordered cards, docs chrome with sidebar and code blocks, public sign-in form.

Captured 2026-11-10, signed out (every captured surface is public; the console behind sign-in was never reached). Themes: dark, light.

A token set and component reference for Appwrite's public site — for building developer-platform marketing and docs surfaces in the style of the real thing. It was read from **appwrite.io** on **2026-11-10**, signed out, in headless Chromium at 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844: the marketing home, pricing, a product page, the docs home and a quick-start, blog, changelog, integrations, company, brand assets, enterprise, startups, and the public sign-in card.

Appwrite is worth a capture because it is a current reference for a dark-pinned developer surface: one `#19191c` ground under everything, a single brand pink (`--brand-cta` #fd366e) reserved for the actions that end a flow, hairline-bordered cards on a translucent muted tint instead of shadows, a Tailwind v4 theme layer with a shadcn-style semantic layer on top, Aeonik Pro marketing type with paired `--text-*` steps, and a docs chrome that is a product in itself.

## Typography

8 styles from `core.typography`. `fontFamily` is the first family of each stack; the full stacks, and properties DESIGN.md has no field for (text case, decoration), are in tokens.json. Families: ui-sans-serif.

### Fonts (from README.md)

**Aeonik Pro** (`--font-aeonik-pro`) is Appwrite's licensed marketing face — every headline, nav item and button on the site. It is not distributed; the style guide falls back to the system sans. **Inter** (`--font-inter`) is the product face, free and substitutable. Code runs on the ui-monospace stack (`--font-mono`); nine `@font-face` rules were recorded in [raw/css-vars.json](raw/css-vars.json).

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do take values from [tokens.json](tokens.json) when you need another theme, a value's source, or a token this file leaves out.
- Do read [README.md](README.md) before relying on a value; it says what is known to be wrong.
- Don't read colours off the screenshots; they are 256-colour PNGs.
- Don't copy the product's logo, icons, illustrations or brand colours into something that ships. Borrow structure and proportions.
- Don't edit this file; it is regenerated from the tokens.

### What to distrust (from README.md)

- **Readings past a masked bot signal.** The committed screenshots and readings were taken with `navigator.webdriver` masked, the flag bot checks read to spot automation. The capture scripts no longer mask it (not run since), so a recapture may record a walled route as a boundary instead of a reading.
- **Dark is painted, light is declared.** Every captured route pins `html.dark`; the `dark` set is measured evidence, the `light` set is the `:root` declaration the console app uses — never seen on these pages.
- **The page lies about devicePixelRatio.** appwrite.io's scripts make `window.devicePixelRatio` read 1 while the renderer paints at 2x; the `.capture.json` sidecars record both (`devicePixelRatio` real, `reportedDevicePixelRatio` the page's).
- **`component.*` tokens live on the dark set only** (the painted theme); they are measured heights/radii, not site variables.
- **Skins are evidence, not themes.** The `.crazy`/`.stealth`/`.premium`/`.high-contrast`/`.barbie`/`.nineties`/`.legacy` blocks are console easter eggs in the shared bundle; binned `skins` in css-vars.json, never tokenised.
- **No icons.** No standalone SVG set was lifted (declared `layoutGaps`); the icon glyphs visible in crops are Appwrite's artwork.
- **Quantised screenshots.** `screenshots/` are 256-colour PNGs; read exact colours from the tokens.

### Do and don't (from README.md)

1. **Do paint the whole marketing surface dark.** `#19191c` ground, `#1d1d21` card, `#222224` border, `#fafafa` text, `#9f9fa9` muted. See [home-dark-default](screenshots/home-dark-default.png).
2. **Do reserve the brand pink for the action that ends a flow.** `--brand-cta` #fd366e marks Sign up, Start project and Login; everything else is ghost or muted. See [signup-button-default](components/crops/signup-button-default.png) and [cta-primary-default](components/crops/cta-primary-default.png).
3. **Do give the hero headline the gradient clip.** Pink to orange through background-clip on the first line only. See [hero-title-default](components/crops/hero-title-default.png).
4. **Do separate surfaces with hairlines, not shadows.** 1px `#222224` borders and the translucent `measured.card-tint` fill carry the cards. See [plan-card-default](components/crops/plan-card-default.png).
5. **Do size controls at 36/40px.** Nav rows, OAuth buttons and fields are 36px with 8px corners; primary CTAs 40px. See [oauth-button-default](components/crops/oauth-button-default.png) and [email-input-default](components/crops/email-input-default.png).
6. **Don't introduce a second accent.** The `--color-*` ramps feed charts, code and status, not UI chrome; the only hue doing work is the pink. See [pricing-dark-default](screenshots/pricing-dark-default.png).
7. **Don't ship the light set as a marketing theme.** It is the console's declared system; the marketing pages never paint it. See [raw/css-vars.json](raw/css-vars.json).
8. **Don't expect the skins to be real themes.** The seven easter-egg palettes are console jokes in the bundle, not user-facing marketing themes.
